issues.where: PRUNE_STEP (lines 18-21, used at line 36); also plugin/README.md:23, paper.md:113, report.md:6
issues.problem: The floater-pruning schedule was moved from the paper's explicit setting to step 6667 based on test-split smoke results. The justification ('the README's 2/3 proportion') is also weaker than it is presented.
issues.evidence: Paper sec/4_experiments.tex:26 says 'Floater pruning is applied once after training completes', and 3_methods.tex:157 says 'at the end of training'. The official code has no default (prune_sched=[]), and the README's 20000-of-30000 is a 30k/-r 2 recipe that differs from the paper's 10k setting in other ways too. In the README run, pruning comes AFTER densification has stopped (densify_until_iter 18000 < 20000), followed by 10k steps of pure optimisation with densify_lag 1e6. At 6667/10000, densification is still active (until 18000) and an opacity reset still happens at 9000, so '2/3' does not reproduce the README's regime either. The choice was made from tools/prune_offline.py, which measures only the TEST split (evidence/smoke-c-noprune/prune_offline.json), on a 2k-step compressed smoke run that does not represent the 10k schedule. Pruning at 2/3 is still net-negative in the smoke run: official range 18.54 vs 18.90 without pruning (-0.37 dB), paper range 18.86 (-0.05 dB). The paper's ablation claims +0.28 dB. Under CLAUDE.md's honesty rules this is a schedule choice made on test images and must be labelled 'tuned'. plan.md:12 still says prune_step '=total 10000', which contradicts the code.
issues.fix: Either (a) make the default prune_step = TOTAL_STEPS (paper) and register the 6667 schedule as a separately named variant labelled 'tuned (chosen on garden test-split 2k smoke)', or (b) keep 6667 but label it 'tuned / deviation selected on test-split smoke' in README, report.md, paper.md and the MethodSpec description, AND add the paper-schedule variant (prune at 10000) to bench_request so both are reported. Correct the '2/3 like the README' wording: the README prunes after densification ends. Fix plan.md:12. If you re-justify the choice, use the validation split, never test.

issues.problem: Headline metric is not defined. The official metric set (metrics.py --exclude_path, render.py renders all cameras of the full scene) is ALL non-training images, i.e. test ∪ validation here. The plugin README presents test (llffhold8 minus train, 19-31 images) as the primary split.
issues.evidence: source/code/metrics.py:24-53 skips only the training filenames. render.py:78 renders scene.getTrainCameras() of the full (non-eval) scene. prepare_m360_sgs12.py:132-133 builds test = idx%8==0 minus train and val = the rest, so test ∪ val = the official set (verified).
issues.fix: State in bench_request/report that the paper-comparable number is the per-view-weighted mean over test ∪ validation (pool the per_view rows, do not average the two split means). Report test-only as the paper-text variant.

issues.problem: The C5 probe accepts pruning of up to 50% of the background wall. The measured paper-mode run removes 304 of 1200 wall Gaussians (25%), so a much more aggressive or wrong range (e.g. also removing Gaussians behind the mode) would still pass. For the default mode_range=official, the probe shows the floater is NOT removed (floaters_left 4, 8 wall Gaussians pruned). Only the index formula is checked for the default.
issues.evidence: ss-verify evidence: paper {pruned 308, floaters_left 0, walls_left 896}; official {pruned 8, floaters_left 4, walls_left 1192}.
issues.fix: Assert that no Gaussian strictly behind the mode at a flagged pixel is pruned in paper mode (compare against an independent per-pixel reference of the [first contributor, mode] set). State explicitly in the report that the default (official) range does not remove the synthetic floater.

issues.problem: CTX.seed uses the config seed (0), not the runtime run seed. CTX.draw_cfg is a module-global set at loss-factory time and is never reset between method builds in one process.
issues.fix: Seed from the run seed if exposed; reset draw_cfg in initialize or build it per method.

issues.problem: The official evaluation resolution is ambiguous and not recorded. The released zips contain full-resolution images (garden 5185x3359). The README trains with -r 2 (1/2 res, not 1/4) and renders without -r, so Inria's loader caps width at 1600 px. The paper says 1/4. Our 1/4 choice follows the paper text but should be listed as a fidelity gap.
The sparsegs-3dgs control still runs the softmax-depth CUDA pass every training step (with_depth defaults to grad-enabled) although no loss uses it. Compute only, results unaffected.
issues.evidence: method_3dgs keeps sparsegs-renderer with no depth consumer.
issues.fix: Optional: config flag to skip the depth pass in the control.

probe_assessment.why: Independent float64 per-pixel reference for forward and all four input gradients, plus a softmax != log-alpha separation check at beta=5. Replacing it with alpha depth, or breaking the backward, fails. Measured rel. grad error <= 3e-6.
Compared with torch.corrcoef; affine/negation invariances; exact patch count; uncorrelated depth must give a high loss.
Identity and known-shift warps, Rodrigues vs scipy with the official sign, masked-L1 formula, and Pearson skipped on warp steps.
Stub UNet/VAE: the latent gradient must equal w(eps_hat - eps); fixed-timestep mapping; ellipse views look at the centre within the z bounds. Does not exercise the real SD weights (acceptable).

A no-op pruner leaves the floater and fails the paper-mode check. But the tolerance (keep >= 50% of the wall) is loose, and in the default official mode the floater survives, so only the index formula is tested there (minor issue).

summary: I checked the implementation against the official code operator by operator and it is faithful. The CUDA softmax/alpha/mode depth forward is identical to forward.cu, and I re-derived the backward independently; it matches an autograd reference to about 1e-6. Pearson, SDS, the warp (including banker's rounding and last-write-wins), warp cameras, ellipse sampling, the warp-render densification statistics, Inria density with min_opacity 0.05, the xyz lr over 30k steps, and the dip-test pruning (official calc_diff, percentile floor 80, power threshold -4, thread-rank index bug) all match. ss-verify passes all 8 probes; pytest 8/8. The dataset split matches the official metric set when test and validation are pooled. One major issue blocks approval: the floater-pruning step was moved from the paper's explicit 'once after training completes' to 6667, a choice made from TEST-split results of a 2k-step compressed smoke run. The 'README 2/3 proportion' rationale ignores that the README prunes after densification has stopped, and pruning is still net-negative at 2/3 in that smoke run. It must be labelled 'tuned' and the paper schedule benchmarked as well, or the default restored to the paper's step.
